page.desc: Six Tesla-style screens for 2014-2018 Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra compared on price, chip, what factory functions survive, warranty and returns, with owner complaints.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best tesla style screen for silverado (2014-2018 Silverado and GMC Sierra) for most owners is the Merge Screens 15.6-inch Premium: $1,299 on 2026-11-06, it keeps OnStar, Bose, the cameras, climate and heated-seat controls on the new screen, and it comes with a 90-day return and a prepaid return label if it cannot be made to work in your truck. If you want the longest warranty, the CarpuTech 14.4-inch Qualcomm Tesla-style screen ({buy:carputech-silverado-sierra-2014-2018-14-4-qualcomm-tesla-screen}) is the only unit in this group with a 2-year warranty, versus 1 year from every rival, on a Snapdragon 665 with Android 13 and wireless CarPlay. It keeps OnStar, the Bose amp and SiriusXM, but its listing does not say whether the backup camera or climate controls carry over, so ask support before you order. The biggest worry in owner threads is fit and lost factory functions, not speed: Phoenix Automotive and AutoTecPro make you pick your factory screen size (4.2, 7 or 8 inch) or OnStar type before checkout, which is the safest way to avoid a unit that does not plug in.

Budget pick: the Phoenix Automotive Special Edition 14.5-inch at $729.99 (2026-11-06) runs Android 14, keeps the physical climate buttons and OnStar, and comes from a Los Angeles company with a 1-year warranty. Best hardware per dollar: the AutoTecPro 15.6-inch QHD at $1,011.69 on sale (2026-11-06) has a 2,560 by 1,440 panel, 8 GB / 128 GB, wireless CarPlay and keeps heated and cooled seat controls, with a 1-year warranty.

page.after:
What owners complain about

Independent owner reports are scattered across truck forums, and most seller pages carry only their own reviews. The themes that repeat:

  • Fit and compatibility is the top complaint. One sponsored F-150 guide says compatibility problems account for most negative reviews in this category, and a GM-Trucks owner said his Tesla-style unit was the third one he tried before one worked. Phoenix sells separate variants for the 4.2, 7 and 8 inch factory screens, and AutoTecPro asks for your OnStar type and a dash photo. CarpuTech's 2014-2018 listing does not ask for your factory screen size.
  • Lost factory functions. In a Ram forum thread on 10.4-inch Tesla-style radios, 3 posters had to rewire the backup camera, 2 lost SiriusXM and 2 lost the factory microphone. A Raptor owner who pulled a Linkswell Gen II unit lost climate behavior, the heated steering wheel and the factory USB port until the stock deck went back in.
  • Software and boot time. One Ram owner's unit boot-looped for 5 to 10 minutes on cold mornings. A Raptor owner reported settings wiped back to FM on every start, and another found boot time about twice the factory deck.
  • Glare. One owner found the screen went black through polarized sunglasses. A Silverado owner added a screen cover for glare.
  • Support. A Ram owner called Phoenix quick to help while another pointed to dozens of Better Business Bureau complaints. The Raptor owner said Linkswell would not stand behind the Gen II unit. A Mercedes owner on MB World called a CarpuTech CarPlay retrofit a mess and returned it.

Which one by need

  • Lowest-risk purchase: Merge Screens 15.6-inch Premium. The 90-day return with a prepaid label covers the fit problem that sinks most buyers, and it has the most owner reviews (48 at 4.7 stars on its own site). Budget for the wireless CarPlay add-on if you want it.
  • Best hardware per dollar: AutoTecPro 15.6-inch QHD at $1,011.69 on sale. It is the only unit here with a 2,560 by 1,440 panel and 8 GB / 128 GB at this price, with wireless CarPlay and heated-seat control kept. Warranty is 1 year.
  • Longest warranty: CarpuTech 14.4-inch Qualcomm. Two years versus one everywhere else, a Snapdragon 665 and wireless CarPlay. Know that AutoTecPro gives more memory and a sharper screen for about $12 more, that CarpuTech's page has no reviews yet, and that non-defect returns cost a 19% restocking fee.
  • Budget: Phoenix Automotive 14.5-inch at $729.99. It keeps the physical climate buttons and OnStar and runs Android 14. Confirm with Phoenix whether CarPlay is built in on your variant, since the page lists a CarPlay module as an optional accessory.
  • Shop-installed with dealer support: Linkswell Gen 6. Sold only through authorized dealers, who handle warranty and tech support.

Not recommended

  • No-name 14.4-inch and 15.6-inch units on eBay shipped from overseas sellers. They list no US warranty, and fitment claims change from listing to listing.
  • CarpuTech's older 15.6-inch non-Qualcomm Silverado listing at $999. It names no processor or Android version, so you cannot tell what you are buying. Pay the extra for the Qualcomm version.
  • Any Tesla-style unit for a truck with aftermarket CAN-bus devices such as tuners or start-stop bypasses. Linkswell warns its radio may not work with them, and other makers do not address it.
